correctness.rationale: Orbifold quotient geodesic distance is the minimum over q round-sphere rotational lifts. In polar coordinates its cosine is cos(theta1)cos(theta2)+sin(theta1)sin(theta2)cos(psi), with independent shortest longitude difference psi uniform [0,pi/q]. For q>=2 cos(psi)>=0, so near-diameter points lie in opposite radius-epsilon polar caps. Summing both orientations and scaling polar radii by epsilon produces the exact factor epsilon^4/(2a) with quadratic domain s^2+t^2+2st cos(psi)<1. The integral I(psi)=(sin(psi)-psi cos(psi))/(8sin^3(psi)) is continuous at zero with I(0)=1/24; exact integration yields the asserted C_q. Monotonicity of the domain proves strict C_q decrease, and q=1 has the familiar spherical cosine-uniform quadratic tail. Independent SciPy quadrature rederived C_q from I for q=2,3,4,6,10,50. The limiting integral, not a finite simulation, proves the asymptotic.
residual_risks: Tail remainder is for each fixed q; no uniform q limit. The q=1 law is separate since all directions have diametral antipodes.

value.rationale: A single simple one-dimensional observable, the near-diameter tail of a natural two-point metric-measure statistic, distinguishes all axial cyclic quotient orders while recovering the radius. The strict coefficient law is a nontrivial intrinsic inverse-statistics result for a canonical family of singular spherical metrics.
residual_risks: Does not characterize general footballs with unequal cone angles, general orbifolds, or arbitrary metrics.

limitations: q>=1 integer axial rotational spherical quotient only, R>0, area-uniform independent points.
